To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human DNA polymerase lambda (Pol λ) can efficiently bypass 2-hydroxyladenine, a common lesion produced by reactive oxidative species, in a sequence-dependent manner and that the fidelity of bypass is enhanced by the auxiliary factors Proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) or replication protein A (RP-A).
the DNA polymerase λ, in combination with the auxiliary factors PCNA and RPA, can bypass the DNA lesion 2-OH adenine in an error-free manner.

the 2-hydroxyl adenine lesion can be efficiently bypassed by human DNA polymerases lambda, delta and epsilon in a sequence context dependent manner, and that the fidelity of bypass is enhanced by proliferating cell nuclear antigen and replication protein A.
In summary, our research is concerned with
DNA damage and repair, in particular the repair of oxidative lesions, and the mechanisms of bypass of these lesions by DNA polymerases.
the mechanisms by which the human DNA polymerase lambda bypasses a common oxidative lesion.

the mechanism of translesion DNA synthesis by the DNA polymerase λ in the presence of the auxiliary proteins PCNA and RP- A and the role of the active site tyrosine residue in the nucleotide selectivities opposite the lesion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

human DNA pol λ, with or without the assistance of auxiliary proteins, can bypass the 2-hydroxylated adenine lesion in a highly error-free manner, and that the type of mispairing observed varies with either the DNA polymerase or the DNA sequence context.
the fidelity of DNA pol λ is dependent on the sequence context of the lesion and the presence of the auxiliary proteins PCNA and RP.A.
2-OH-dA is not a strong block for the DNA pols tested, and that the type of misincorporation opposite this lesion is dependent on the DNA pol, the sequence context and the auxiliary protein(s).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2-hydroxyl group in adenine can be bypassed with high fidelity by DNA pol λ, but the sequence context of the lesion is a determinant of the fidelity of the reaction.
the bypass of 2-oxoadenosine lesions by DNA polymerases can occur in a sequence context and auxiliary protein-dependent fashion.
the bypass of 2-oxo- and 2-hydroxypurines by DNA pol λ is highly dependent on sequence context, and that this is modulated by the auxiliary proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 2-hydroxylated adenine can be bypassed by DNA pol λ in a sequence context-dependent manner, with PCNA and RPA enhancing the fidelity of translesional synthesis.
the sequence context of a lesion can have a significant impact on the fidelity of translesional synthesis.
the sequence context of the lesion and the presence of auxiliary proteins can determine the efficiency and fidelity of bypass of a DNA lesion.
